title: General Chemistry I & II
description: Builds quantitative problem-solving and molecular-level reasoning across measurement, atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, aqueous reactions, gases, thermochemistry, and intermolecular forces—the chemical foundations needed for biology, engineering, environmental science, and later chemistry courses.

topics.title: Course Orientation, Measurement, Matter, and Laboratory Foundations
topics.description: This opening unit establishes chemistry as a quantitative and experimental science. Students learn how to measure, report, classify, and reason about matter before tackling molecular models.

children.title: Measurement and Units
children.description: Students learn the measurement language needed for every chemistry calculation.

children.title: Classification of Matter
children.description: Classifying matter helps students connect observations to particle-level explanations.

children.title: Laboratory Skills and Safety
children.description: Lab practice teaches careful measurement, uncertainty, and safe experimental habits.

children.title: Accuracy, precision, error, and data reporting

topics.title: Atoms, Isotopes, and the Periodic Table
topics.description: This unit introduces atoms as the basic building blocks of chemical identity. Students learn how subatomic particles, isotopes, and the periodic table organize matter.

children.title: Atomic Structure
children.description: Students learn what atoms contain and how subatomic particles determine identity and charge.

children.title: Isotopes and Atomic Mass
children.description: Isotopes explain why atomic masses on the periodic table are weighted averages.

children.title: Periodic Table Organization
children.description: Students learn how the table groups elements by recurring properties.

topics.title: Electronic Structure and Quantum Theory of the Atom
topics.description: This unit explains how electrons are arranged and why that arrangement controls chemical behavior. It gives the conceptual basis for periodic trends and bonding.

children.title: Light, Energy, and Quantization
children.description: Students see why atomic spectra require a quantum model of energy.

children.title: Bohr model as a stepping stone
Orbitals and Electron Configurations
children.description: Students learn how electrons occupy orbitals in atoms.

children.title: Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion, Hund's rule
Valence Electrons
children.description: Valence electrons connect atomic structure to reactivity and bonding.

topics.title: Periodic Trends and Chemical Periodicity
topics.description: Periodic trends let students predict properties before memorizing facts. This unit turns the periodic table into an explanatory model.

children.title: Effective Nuclear Charge and Shielding
children.description: These ideas explain why electron attraction changes across the table.

children.title: Atomic and Ionic Radii
children.description: Students learn why atom and ion sizes vary systematically.

children.title: Ionization Energy, Electron Affinity, and Electronegativity
children.description: These properties predict ion formation, bond polarity, and reactivity.

topics.title: Chemical Nomenclature, Formulas, and Composition
topics.description: This unit teaches students to name substances, interpret formulas, and calculate composition. It is the language bridge between chemical symbols and chemical quantities.

children.title: Chemical Formulas
children.description: Students learn how formulas encode composition and charge balance.

children.title: Nomenclature
children.description: Naming rules help students communicate substances precisely.

children.title: Moles and Composition
children.description: The mole links atomic-scale formulas to measurable laboratory amounts.

topics.title: Chemical Bonding: Ionic, Covalent, and Metallic Models
topics.description: Bonding explains why atoms combine and what properties result. Students learn the major bonding models and where each one works best.

children.title: Ionic Bonding
children.description: Students learn how electron transfer and electrostatic attraction form ionic compounds.

children.title: Covalent Bonding
children.description: Students learn how shared electrons form molecules.

children.title: Metallic Bonding
children.description: Metallic bonding explains conductivity, malleability, and alloy behavior.

topics.title: Lewis Structures, Resonance, Formal Charge, and Bond Polarity
topics.description: This unit gives students a visual model for molecular connectivity and electron placement. It prepares them for geometry, polarity, and reactivity.

children.title: Lewis Structure Construction
children.description: Students learn a repeatable method for drawing valid electron-dot structures.

children.title: Formal Charge and Resonance
children.description: Formal charge and resonance help students compare plausible structures.

children.title: Bond Polarity
children.description: Students connect electronegativity differences to partial charges.

topics.title: Molecular Geometry, VSEPR, Hybridization, and Molecular Polarity
topics.description: This unit turns flat Lewis structures into three-dimensional molecules. Students learn how shape controls polarity, properties, and interactions.

children.title: VSEPR Shapes
children.description: Students learn how electron groups arrange to reduce repulsion.

children.title: Linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral geometries
Hybridization
children.description: Hybridization gives a bonding-language shortcut for common molecular shapes.

children.title: Molecular Polarity
children.description: Students learn to combine bond dipoles and geometry to predict whole-molecule polarity.

topics.title: Stoichiometry and Chemical Equations
topics.description: Stoichiometry is the quantitative heart of Chemistry I. Students learn to use balanced equations to connect substances, amounts, and reaction outcomes.

children.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
children.description: Balanced equations express conservation of atoms.

children.title: Interpreting equations in particles and moles
Mole-to-Mole and Mass Calculations
children.description: Students learn how equations become calculation maps.

children.title: Limiting Reactants and Yield
children.description: These ideas connect ideal reaction calculations to real lab results.

topics.title: Aqueous Reactions and Solution Stoichiometry
topics.description: This unit brings reactions into water, where many biological, environmental, and laboratory systems operate. Students learn ions, concentrations, and reaction types.

children.title: Solutions and Concentration
children.description: Students learn how amount and volume describe dissolved substances.

children.title: Precipitation, Acid-Base, and Redox Reactions
children.description: Reaction categories help students predict products and interpret observations.

children.title: Net Ionic Equations and Titration
children.description: Students learn to focus on chemical change and quantify reactions in solution.

topics.title: Gases and Gas Laws
topics.description: Gas behavior shows how particle models become useful equations. Students connect pressure, volume, temperature, and moles to molecular motion.

children.title: Gas Variables and Laws
children.description: Students learn how gas properties vary under controlled conditions.

children.title: Boyle's, Charles's, Avogadro's, and combined gas laws
Ideal Gas Law and Stoichiometry
children.description: The ideal gas law links gas measurements to moles and reaction quantities.

children.title: Molar mass and density of gases
Kinetic Molecular Theory and Real Gases
children.description: Students learn why gas laws work and when they fail.

children.title: Deviations at high pressure and low temperature

topics.title: Thermochemistry and Energy Changes
topics.description: Thermochemistry explains heat flow in chemical and physical processes. Students learn to quantify energy changes and connect them to bonds and reactions.

children.title: Heat, Work, and Enthalpy
children.description: Students learn energy vocabulary and the meaning of enthalpy change.

children.title: Calorimetry
children.description: Calorimetry connects temperature changes to heat transfer.

children.title: Hess's Law and Bond Energies
children.description: Students learn alternate ways to calculate reaction enthalpy.

topics.title: States of Matter, Intermolecular Forces, and Phase Behavior
topics.description: This unit explains why substances have different boiling points, solubilities, vapor pressures, and physical states. It connects molecular structure to macroscopic properties.

children.title: Intermolecular Forces
children.description: Students learn the attractions between particles that determine many physical properties.

children.title: Liquids and Solids
children.description: Students connect particle arrangement to properties of condensed phases.

children.title: Phase Changes and Diagrams
children.description: Phase diagrams summarize how temperature and pressure control physical state.

topics.title: Integrated Chemistry I Applications and Lab Synthesis
topics.description: The final unit consolidates the course through applications and lab-style synthesis. Students practice choosing models, checking calculations, and communicating chemical reasoning.

children.title: Cumulative Problem Solving
children.description: Students learn to recognize which chemistry model a problem calls for.

children.title: Combining stoichiometry, gases, solutions, and energy
Laboratory Data and Error Analysis
children.description: Students connect experiments to chemical claims.

children.title: Lab report claims, evidence, and reasoning
Applications Across Fields
children.description: Students see how Chemistry I supports later work in science, health, engineering, and environment.
